sections.h2: What towns and landmarks make up Greene County?
sections.html:
Greene County sits in east central Georgia, in the part of the state called the Lake country, and Greensboro serves as seat and largest city. Lawmakers formed it on February 3, 1786 from Washington County land, and the name honors Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene (Wikipedia).

Of 406 square miles in total, 387 are land and 19, or 4.6%, are water. Streams drain three ways: the Oconee River across the west, the Little River toward the Savannah in the north, and the Ogeechee in the south. A piece of the Oconee National Forest lies inside the line, and the extinct river town of Scull Shoals recalls the county's earlier years. Interstate 20 runs through, with US 278 and State Routes 12, 15, 44 and 77 as other main roads.

The incorporated places are Greensboro, Union Point, White Plains, Woodville and the town of Siloam, and Bairdstown is an unincorporated community. Oglethorpe, Taliaferro, Hancock, Putnam, Morgan and Oconee counties ring it. Local families can choose among the Greene County School Board, Lake Oconee Academy and Nathanael Greene Academy. Whether the house is lakeside or in town, the tax commissioner's office sends the bill, so the steps below apply across the county.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Greene County owners?
sections.html:
Greene County went from 18,915 people in the 2020 census to an estimated 21,367 in July 2025, a gain of 13.0%. Residents 65 and over make up 33.5% of the population, a full third, so the senior exemptions listed further down reach a large share of local owners. Wikipedia links recent growth to people moving to Reynolds Lake Oconee.

sections.h2: Where do Greene County property tax questions go?
sections.html:
Both offices share one address on Silver Drive in Greensboro. The tax commissioner bills and collects on real and personal property, mobile homes, vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues tags as a state agent. The tax assessors set values, take returns and approve exemptions.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101 at 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, with the lobby open weekdays from 8 am until 4:45 pm.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 at the same address, phone 706-453-3355, for values, appeals and homestead filings.
  • Online: the county publishes a homestead application page and a digest and assessments page for the current year.

Hours and forms are posted on the commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page.

sections.h2: What is the Greene County tax deadline?
sections.html:
Greene County bills come due on December 1, shifting to the next business day when that date lands on a weekend or holiday. The commissioner's page cautions that land with unpaid tax can be levied upon and in time sold.

The surrounding calendar follows a set pattern. A return covers property owned on January 1 and is accepted through April 1. A real property return carries over each year at the earlier value, while personal property needs a fresh return annually. For mobile homes the state's county facts sheet says the owner returns the home for tax by April 1 and applies for the yearly location permit between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices tend to go out around May, and the commissioners and the school board set millage rates later in the year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?
sections.html:
A property owner has 45 days from the mailing date of the notice. The appeal may rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and it is written on the state's uniform form, PT-311A, and filed with the Board of Tax Assessors. That first filing must also say which route you want.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors look first and may mail an amended notice, which you can contest within 30 days; an appeal they leave as is advances to a Board of Equalization hearing, with Superior Court after that.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser rules on value, available only for non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.
  • Arbitration: you supply a current certified appraisal, and the assessors may accept or reject it; a rejected one goes to the clerk of Superior Court, a hearing follows within 30 days, and the arbitrator's ruling is final.

The county page explains each route in more detail and points to the Department of Revenue site for forms.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Greene County use?
sections.html:
For a given year you need to have owned and lived in the home on January 1 and to file by April 1; a later filing waits a year. Once granted, the exemption renews until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, the state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, described as $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64 with net income of $10,000 at most: $2,000 on county taxes and $10,000 on school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over with net income of $10,000 at most: $12,000 on county taxes and $18,000 on school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, a 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and needs proof.

A trailing F on a code, as in S1F, flags the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value since the day the exemption was approved. The county says the freeze covers the house and up to five acres, and leaves out pools, barns, detached garages and shops (county homestead page). The county also describes a deferral program for owners 62 and over with household income of $15,000 or less, and farmland that qualifies can be assessed at 30%.

sections.h2: What should a Greene County seller do about tax before closing?
sections.html:
The Georgia Department of Revenue says an owner on January 1 stays responsible for that whole year even when the sale happens on January 2, and no refund is paid for part of a year. A purchase contract normally splits the bill, so the figure that counts is the exact balance on the parcel.

Request a statement of what is owed for this year and earlier ones from the commissioner's office. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should send. Keep the assessment notice and any appeal paperwork in the file, since a pending appeal can alter the final bill. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the next owner can apply in their name.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Greene County property tax?
faqs.a: December 1, or the next business day if that date lands on a weekend or holiday. The commissioner's page adds that property with unpaid tax may be levied upon and eventually sold.

faqs.q: What is the window to contest a Greene County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and say whether you want the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: By what date must I file Greene County homestead paperwork?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current tax year, and you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1. A later application is held until the following year.

faqs.q: What does the code S1F mean on a Greene County notice?
faqs.a: The F marks the homestead freeze, an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the level on the day your homestead was approved. The county says it reaches the house and up to five acres, and leaves out pools, barns, detached garages and shops.

faqs.q: Which Greene County office do I phone about a bill or a value?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at 706-453-3358 about bills and payments, and the tax assessors at 706-453-3355 about values, appeals and exemptions. Both work from 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.
